material_findings.supported_finding: The entire shortlist leaves undo as unspecified, application-defined, or future investigation. Its one concrete undo trace is a product-policy question, not a discovery of how an implementation can selectively reverse tracked operations. The primary Yjs API documents a scoped selective inverse-operation stack, origin tracking, and edit-grouping controls. These capabilities bear directly on the proposed one-undo-after-sync trace and differ from restoring an earlier whole-note snapshot.
material_findings.materiality: Undo is expressly inside the assigned bounded aspect. Leaving every implementation capability unknown deprives the mechanism comparison and prospective undo test of the distinction between selecting whose operations to reverse and reverting shared state. This is missing role discovery, not a requirement to choose the desired product policy, prove all cross-device behavior, deploy software, or execute a test.
material_findings.qualification: The candidate honestly documents the failed retrieval and does not falsely claim Yjs lacks undo. The failure is acknowledged; nevertheless, uncertainty about the desired product policy does not cover the omitted discoverable capability. The independently retrieved official Markdown rendition supplies bounded primary evidence. No particular API or exhaustive undo survey is mandated; this API establishes why the absent semantic distinction matters.
material_findings.disposition: Retain supported mechanism discoveries; the role source judgment fails for this material coverage omission. No candidate changes or feedback supplied.

limitations.detail: The CRDT paragraph makes Yjs update/garbage-collection claims but its trailing citations list S1-S3. S4 elsewhere in the saved map supports them.

Git retaining base and both sides of an unresolved repository merge is true, but S7 is the standalone merge-file manual. Independent P9 TRUE MERGE gives the precise repository-index precedent. The candidate explicitly treats this as a precedent rather than a ready-made workflow.

Automatic only for non-overlapping is a coarse boundary: identical changes by both sides may be resolved cleanly. The prose and next step do not make a consequential rejection or promise based on that simplification.

useful_discoveries.detail: Automerge operation granularity matters: infrequent whole-string diff conversion can merge poorly, making per-keystroke versus splice an actionable adapter check.
Yjs compressed update merging and deletion garbage collection are different operations; measure loaded-document cleanup rather than assuming mergeUpdates shrinks away deleted content.
ShareDB is operation machinery plus an OT type, so offline support alone does not establish the note-text transform or undo contract.
RCS-style line merging and explicit retained revision adoption preserve meaningful human-resolution alternatives to automatic operation merge.
Yjs supplies origin-scoped selective undo and 500 ms capture grouping, so one undo need not mean one keystroke; source capability and desired product policy are separate.

Git endpoint/base merging does not replay individual edits: an edit later reverted on one branch may reappear on merging another branch. This reinforces the need to distinguish history inspection from operation-aware undo.
